methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $6.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $8.6B.

data.narrative:
Nuro, a Series G autonomous delivery company founded by Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu, is valued at $6.0B post-money after raising $2.54B to date. The valuation assessment relies on a peer set of four same-sector comparables spanning late-stage private and public companies: Wayve ($8.6B, Series D), Zipline ($7.6B, Series H), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B, public). The broader drones and autonomous mobility sector includes six evaluated private companies with significant capital commitments.

Two valuation methods triangulate to a range. Stage-progression analysis applies a standard 1.25x step-up multiplier to the $6.0B Series G post-money valuation, implying $7.5B at the next funding stage. Peer-median methodology yields $7.2B, derived from the four-company comp median, with a peer range spanning $3.3B to $8.6B. These methods show modest dispersion, with only $300M separating the two point estimates.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B (low) to $8.6B (high), with a median of $7.4B. This places Nuro slightly above its last round valuation, consistent with stage progression expectations. Key uncertainties include heterogeneity within the peer set—regulatory approval timelines, revenue generation models, and path to profitability vary materially across autonomous delivery versus air taxi verticals—and limited public market comparables in this nascent sector.
